Article Title: 0%, 100%, then 200%: How Trump's new generic drug tariff plan could hit India
Article Text:
What it means for India

President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced a phased tariff plan for imported generic medicines, saying they would continue to enter US duty-free for the next two years before attracting tariffs of up to 200%.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said generic medicines imported into the US would continue to attract zero tariffs from August 1, 2026, for two years, after which the duty would rise to 100% for one year and 200% thereafter."Effective August 1st, 2026, all Generic Drugs being brought into the United States will continue to have a tariff of zero percent for two years, after which the tariff will be raised to 100 per cent for one year, and 200 per cent thereafter," Trump said."This is done in order to RESHORE Generic Pharmaceutical Production into America, with a penalty to those Companies that decide not to build Plant and Equipment within the stated period of time given to them," he added.Trump said the policy was designed to strengthen domestic manufacturing and protect American consumers. "The Policy on Patented, Branded, or Innovative Drugs, which has been so successful, will remain as is," he noted.The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) estimates that generic medicines account for more than 90% of all prescriptions dispensed in the country, according to PTI.The announcement is significant for India, often referred to as the "pharmacy of the world" because of its large-scale production of affordable generic medicines.According to a Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) report, India exported $9.7 billion worth of pharmaceuticals to the US in 2025, accounting for 38% of its total pharmaceutical exports of $25.8 billion.Indian generic medicines are widely prescribed in the US to treat conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, cancer, infectious diseases and mental health disorders.According to healthcare analytics firm IQVIA, Indian pharmaceutical companies supply 47% of all generic prescriptions filled at US pharmacies.Their role extends beyond volume, Indian-made generics are estimated to have saved the US healthcare system $219 billion in 2022 alone and $1.3 trillion over the past decade.Indian drugmakers, including Cipla, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries and Dr Reddy's Laboratories, have become major suppliers in the US market.In 2022, they accounted for more than half of the prescriptions by volume in five of the top 10 therapeutic categories, including medicines for high cholesterol, hypertension, depression, ulcers and nervous system disorders, according to an earlier TOI report.Some of the most commonly prescribed Indian-made generic medicines in the US include Metformin for diabetes, Atorvastatin for high cholesterol, Losartan for high blood pressure, and antibiotics such as Amoxicillin and Ciprofloxacin.The proposed tariff regime is part of Trump's broader strategy to bring pharmaceutical manufacturing back to the United States and reduce reliance on imported medicines. It follows earlier measures that encouraged branded drugmakers to manufacture in the US or lower prices in exchange for tariff exemptions.The move also comes as the Trump administration prepares another round of tariffs targeting dozens of countries, including India, with the temporary 10% blanket tariff on imports due to expire later this week.According to the Financial Times, Washington is considering fresh tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from around 60 countries, citing concerns over alleged forced labour practices and unfair trade policies.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Tuesday said additional tariff measures could be announced soon. "The US has laws to prohibit trading goods with forced labour. Other countries, most don't have a law; those that do don't really enforce it," Greer told CNBC."We expect to see some action soon," he added.The latest announcement comes even as Washington and New Delhi have repeatedly said they are close to finalising a bilateral trade agreement, adding fresh uncertainty to trade relations between the two countries.
Article Summary: President Donald Trump announced a phased tariff plan for imported generic medicines. Indian-made generics are estimated to have saved the US healthcare system $219 billion in 2022 alone. Indian drugmakers, including Cipla, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries and Dr Reddy's Laboratories, have become major suppliers in the US market.

Article Title: Crude continues rally: Brent tops $92, WTI above $85 as Strait of Hormuz tensions threaten global supplies
Article Text: Crude oil prices extended their rally on Wednesday, with Brent crude holding above the $90-a-barrel mark as escalating tensions in the Middle East kept investors focused on the risk of further disruptions to global energy supplies.Brent crude was trading at $92.40 a barrel, up 1.53% or $1.39, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 1.38% or $1.16 to $85.50 a barrel.The gains came after both benchmarks ended Tuesday at their highest closing levels in around five weeks. Brent settled at $91.01 a barrel and WTI at $84.91, each rising about 2% during the session as geopolitical developments added to supply concerns.The momentum comes as the Middle East crisis involving the United States, Iran and the Iran-backed Houthis has intensified. Earlier this week, the Houthis announced a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, expanding concerns over disruptions to energy supplies and trade routes.Shipping activity has already been affected. Two tankers carrying Saudi crude destined for China and India changed course in the Red Sea after the Houthi threats and headed back towards the Suez Canal, according to LSEG shipping data cited by Reuters. Despite this, Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export terminal at Yanbu was reported to be operating normally.Military action also continued overnight. US forces struck targets in southern and western Iran, while Iran targeted US sites in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan. At least one tanker was also hit in the Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy shipping route.Beyond the Middle East, another supply risk emerged after the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended receiving oil from Kazakhstan following attacks on oil tankers at its Black Sea terminal. Russia blamed Ukraine for the attacks, while Ukraine did not comment.Separately, data from the Joint Organizations Data Initiative showed Saudi Arabia's crude exports fell for the third consecutive month in May, reaching a record low.Markets are now looking ahead to US inventory data for fresh direction. Analysts expect crude stockpiles to have fallen by 0.5 million barrels in the week ended July 17. If confirmed, it would mark a second straight weekly decline. The comparable week last year recorded a draw of 3.2 million barrels, while the average decline over the past five years was 1.2 million barrels.The impact of the conflict is also being felt beyond energy markets. A United Nations report released on Tuesday projected that more than 500 million people could still face chronic hunger by 2030 despite recent improvements, with Africa expected to account for the largest share.International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) President Alvaro Lario warned that prolonged disruptions to shipping and energy supplies could worsen food insecurity. According to AP, the expert had also warned that if uncertaility continues, including around the Strait of Hormuz, could leave an additional 9 million to 18 million people facing hunger.Meanwhile, the Middle East has continued to boil with US and Iran once again launching strikes. The crisis that began on February 28 had already pushed crude higher to $126 per barrel from the $70 per barrel price, though prices cooled after both sides signed the now breached interim peace deal.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $92.40 a barrel on Wednesday, up 1.53%. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 1.38% or $1.16 to $85.50 a barrel. Gains came after both benchmarks ended Tuesday at their highest closing levels in around five weeks.

Article Title: Hormuz disruptions: India’s crude oil imports from Russia remain near all-time high in July despite no sanctions waiver from US
Article Text:
Russia has strengthened its position as India's largest crude oil supplier. (File PTI photo of Russian oil tanker)

India’s top crude oil suppliers

India’s crude oil imports from Russia continue to be near record highs in July, despite the Donald Trump administration not extending a sanctions waiver. Amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict, Russia has emerged as the key crude oil supplier for India.Some Middle East countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia continue to show supply resilience through alternative routes due to the Strait of Hormuz closure.According to Kpler, a global real-time data and analytics provider, India’s crude oil imports from Russia in July so far have averaged at around 2.45 million barrels per day. This is near the all-time high levels of 2.64 million barrels per day seen in June this year.UAE ranks second with an average supply of 617,000 barrels per day in July so far, and Saudi Arabia is the third largest supplier with India’s average imports from the destination being 586,000 barrels per day in the first few weeks of July.Russia has strengthened its position as India's largest crude oil supplier, with shipments of almost 300 million barrels during the four and a half months since the US-Iran conflict began.Crude sourced from the Middle East through alternative shipping routes continues to account for a significant share of India's imports. Since March, the UAE and Saudi Arabia have ranked as the country's second and third largest suppliers, respectively. Venezuela has also expanded its presence and now features among India's top five crude suppliers.Industry experts say India's crude procurement pattern during the US-Iran conflict reflects a flexible and well-diversified sourcing strategy.Sumit Ritolia, Lead analyst, Modelling and Refining has in the past said: India has arguably been one of the best-positioned major importers, successfully maintaining crude inflows through proactive diversification and procurement strategies.”According to him, import data demonstrates this resilience, with India's crude purchases from alternative suppliers remaining strong despite supply disruptions affecting parts of the Middle East.He added that Indian refiners have effectively secured replacement cargoes while maintaining favourable refinery economics.Before February 2022, Russian oil accounted for barely 2% of India's crude import basket. Between 2023 and 2025, however, it became the country's largest source of crude, contributing roughly one-third of total imports, supported by discounts that at their peak ranged between $15 and $30 per barrel.
Article Summary: India’s crude oil imports from Russia continue to be near record highs in July. Despite the ongoing US-Iran conflict, Russia has emerged as the key crude oil supplier for India. Some Middle East countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia continue to show supply resilience through alternative routes.

Article Title: Asian stocks trade in green: Kospi adds 6%, Nikkei jumps over 1,100 points
Article Text: Asian equities opened higher on Wednesday, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street as investors looked past rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and focused instead on a rebound in technology stocks.The gains were led by Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.Japan's Nikkei climbed 1.30% or 861.21 points to 67,093.4, while South Korea's Kospi surged 4.78% or 322.54 points to 7,070.49 around 9:30 am IST. Taiwan's benchmark index advanced 1.75% or 775.43 points to 45,008.3.In China, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.50% or 19.217 points to 3,883.584, while the Shenzhen Composite gained 0.61% or 87.622 points to 14,351.914. However, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index (HSI) fell 0.73% or 183.24 points to 24,949.05. Back at home, Nifty 50 began in red, slipping 0.15% or 37.25 points to 24,150.45.The broader rally came despite another rise in oil prices after two tankers carrying Saudi crude to Asia reversed course in the Red Sea on Tuesday following threats from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels. Brent crude climbed 0.6% to $91.55 a barrel, extending gains after settling at a five-week high in the previous session.Meanwhile, Wall Street had ended higher overnight, with the S&P 500 rising 0.9% to snap a three-day losing streak. The rebound was driven by semiconductor shares after data showed Korean semiconductor exports nearly tripled during the first few weeks of July, while a measure of Taiwanese export orders for June exceeded estimates.Chipmakers and data storage firms led the gains. SanDisk and Western Digital each rose more than 7% in early trade, while Marvell Technology and Intel gained 6.2% and 5.7%, respectively. Nvidia added 1.3% after disclosing it had acquired a 9% stake in Dutch cloud computing company Nebius.Outside the technology sector, General Motors rose 1.7% after reporting second-quarter sales and profit that beat Wall Street expectations and raising its guidance.Investor attention is now turning to earnings from Alphabet and Tesla. Alphabet is under increased scrutiny over the delayed launch of a model central to its artificial intelligence strategy, while Tesla is widely expected to report its first quarterly cash burn in more than two years as spending on AI and robotics increases.Pharmaceutical stocks are also expected to remain in focus after US President Donald Trump announced that all generic drugs imported into the United States would face a 0% tariff for two years from August 1. The tariff would then rise to 100% for one year and 200% thereafter.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six major peers, stayed close to a one-week high at 101.20. Against the Japanese yen, the dollar slipped 0.1% to 163.06 yen after touching a four-decade high against the currency a day earlier.Bond and currency markets remained largely steady despite higher oil prices ahead of central bank meetings next week. According to the median forecast of economists in a Reuters poll, the US Federal Reserve is expected to leave its key interest rate unchanged for the remainder of 2026, although economists said the likelihood of a rate increase remains high.The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was up 0.2 basis point at 4.628%. Gold rose 0.5% to $4,097.67 an ounce.
Article Summary: Japan's Nikkei climbed 1.30% or 861.21 points to 67,093.4. South Korea's Kospi surged 4.78% or 322.54 points to 7,070.49. Taiwan's benchmark index advanced 1.75% or 775.43 points to 45,008.3. Shanghai Composite rose 0.50% or 19.217 points to 3,883.584.

Article Title: SBI Funds Management listing makes some employees crorepatis; stock debuts at 7% premium to IPO price
Article Text:
SBI Funds Management entered the stock market after attracting robust institutional demand.

Crorepatis from SBI Funds Management listing bonanza



SBI Funds Management stock listing: Years of employee stock ownership at SBI Funds Management is poised to generate multi-crore wealth for several executives as the country's largest asset management company enters the stock market. Based on the IPO issue price of Rs 574 per share, 13 employees own equity stakes valued at more than Rs 1 crore.SBI Funds Management made a strong debut on Dalal Street today, listing at a premium of around 7% over its IPO price. The stock opened at Rs 610 on the BSE, which is a gain of 6.27% from the issue price of Rs 574, while it listed at Rs 613.30 on the NSE.Deputy Managing Director Devinder Pal Singh stands to gain the most, with his vested shareholding valued at around Rs 121 crore, according to the company's prospectus. The next largest holding belongs to Chief Investment Officer Srinivasan Rama Iyer, whose stake is worth about Rs 105 crore, according to an ET report.At the IPO price, Singh's 21.14 lakh vested shares are valued at nearly Rs 121 crore. In addition, he owns unvested stock options that could be worth about Rs 30 crore if exercised in the future. Iyer's 18.25 lakh vested shares have an estimated value of around Rs 105 crore, while his unvested options are valued at roughly Rs 51 crore at the offer price.Several other senior executives are also in line for substantial gains. Chief of Strategy, Digital & Technology and Head of Investor Relations Srinivas Jain holds vested shares worth close to Rs 59 crore.Chief Investment Officer – Fixed Income Rajeev Radhakrishnan has holdings valued at about Rs 36 crore, while Chief Risk Officer Aparna Nirgude's vested stake is worth approximately Rs 31 crore.Chief Compliance Officer, Company Secretary and Head of Legal Vinaya Datar owns vested shares with an estimated value of around Rs 21 crore, the report said.The list of employee shareholders also includes senior leaders from finance, human resources, technology and fund management. Among them are Chief Financial Officer Inderjeet Ghuliani, Chief Human Resources Officer Rajat Grover, Chief Information Security Officer Sanjay Pugaonkar, and fund managers Mohan Lal and Mahesh Chhabria, each of whom holds vested shares worth more than Rs 1 crore at the IPO issue price.Originally launched in 2018 and revised subsequently, the ESOP programme allotted options with exercise prices ranging from about Rs 39 to Rs 455 per share. With the IPO priced at Rs 574 per share, employees who remained with the company through its expansion have realised significant gains on these grants.The company entered the market after attracting robust institutional demand. Ahead of the IPO opening, SBI Funds raised nearly Rs 2,663 crore from anchor investors, with 129 marquee institutions—including BlackRock and Goldman Sachs—participating in the allocation. It had also secured approximately Rs 1,880 crore through a pre-IPO placement.Investor interest remained strong throughout the three-day subscription period from July 14 to July 16. The issue was subscribed nearly 42 times overall, driven primarily by qualified institutional buyers, whose portion was oversubscribed around 140 times. The non-institutional investor category saw subscriptions of 22.51 times, while the retail segment was subscribed 3.6 times.
Article Summary: SBI Funds Management made a strong debut on Dalal Street today, listing at a premium of around 7% over its IPO price. The stock opened at Rs 610 on the BSE, which is a gain of 6.27% from the issue price of Rs 574. The company entered the market after attracting robust institutional demand.

Article Title: Rupee falls 11 paise to 96.36 against US dollar amid US-Iran tensions, rising crude prices
Article Text: Rupee came under pressure in early trade on Wednesday, opening 11 paise lower at 96.36 against the US dollar. The slump came as rising crude oil prices and increased demand for safe-haven assets weighed down the currency.Earlier on Tuesday, rupee had ended at 96.25 against the greenback before slipping at the opening of the interbank foreign exchange market.Market participants attributed the weakness to renewed geopolitical tensions that have kept energy markets on edge. Forex traders said worries over the security of oil shipments through the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz continue to underpin crude prices.They added that Houthi threats against shipping, along with continuing US-Iran hostilities, have sustained the geopolitical risk premium in the market.Even as the dollar index edged 0.01% lower to 101.15, it continued to attract demand as investors sought safer assets following the latest escalation in the US-Iran conflict.Oil prices also remained firm, with Brent crude, the global benchmark, rising 1.18 per cent to USD 92.08 a barrel in futures trade.While external factors exerted pressure on the rupee, recent measures by the Reserve Bank of India to attract overseas deposits have helped cushion the domestic currency, according to Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director at Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP."RBI’s measures to attract overseas deposits have generated significant foreign currency inflows, boosting market confidence and providing support to the rupee," Bhansali said.He added that dealers are closely monitoring whether the RBI intervenes through state-owned banks to contain excessive volatility in the currency market."The central bank appears to be allowing gradual adjustments while preventing disorderly moves," he said.Meanwhile, Dalal Street was also trading in red with BSE Sensex down 0.52% to 77,070.61 and NSE Nifty50 plunging 0.34% at 24,104.40. Exchange data showed that Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) remained net buyers on Tuesday, purchasing equities worth Rs 1,650.16 crore.
Article Summary: Rupee opens 11 paise lower at 96.36 against the US dollar. Rise in crude oil prices and increased demand for safe-haven assets weighed down the currency. BSE Sensex down 0.52% to 77,070.61 and NSE Nifty50 plunging 0.34% at 24,104.40.

Article Title: New worry for oil market: Tankers carrying Saudi crude for India, China make a U-turn in Red Sea on Houthi threats
Article Text:
The Houthis control northern Yemen, including the coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. (Satellite image of Bab el-Mandeb by Reuters)

Saudi Arabia crude takes a U-Turn

Rising risks

Crucial energy bottlenecks at the centre of Middle East crisis

Red Sea oil supply disruptions have begun! Three tankers carrying Saudi Arabia crude oil that were bound for China and India reversed course in the Red Sea on Tuesday. They are now steering toward the Suez Canal instead of continuing along the Yemeni coastline near the entrance to the sea. The change in route followed a warning issued by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia, according to a Reuters report.On Monday, the Houthis announced a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, potentially opening another front in the US-Israeli conflict with Iran and increasing risks to global energy supplies and international trade beyond the Gulf region.In an email sent to shipping companies, the group warned them against loading or unloading cargo at Saudi ports, stating that vessels involved in such operations could be targeted "in ⁠any location".Also Read | Another oil shock loading for India? How Red Sea route disruptions may hit not only Saudi, but also Russian crude supply The Houthis control northern Yemen, including the coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. With the Strait of Hormuz—which provides access to the Gulf—blocked during the conflict, Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu has become the primary alternative export route for Middle Eastern crude, enabling the shipment of millions of barrels of oil each day.The vessels—Xin Long Yang, Rodos and Amazon—turning back point to a potential second disruption along a key global shipping corridor, adding to concerns over energy supplies already affected by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.Shipping data showed that the Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) Xin Long Yang, which loaded 2 million barrels of Saudi crude at Yanbu on Monday, was initially sailing toward China via the southern exit of the Red Sea before reversing course and heading north toward the Suez Canal.The data also showed that Rodos, a smaller tanker carrying around 700,000 barrels of Saudi crude destined for India, changed course toward Suez on Tuesday. The Suezmax tanker Amazon, which loaded Saudi crude for India on Tuesday, also altered its route and headed toward the canal. All three vessels switched off their transponders on Tuesday.Dynacom Tankers Management, which manages Rodos and Amazon, and Cosco Shipping, the manager of Xin Long Yang, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Another VLCC, New Prime, which had been due to reach Yanbu later this week to load crude, also turned back off the coast of Oman before entering the Red Sea. Its manager, Associated Maritime Co HK, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Insurance industry sources told Reuters that war-risk insurance premiums have already increased over the past 24 hours as underwriters reassess the risks associated with Saudi ports."Vessels calling at Saudi Arabian ports are advised to reconsider transiting the Red Sea and to consider implementing enhanced mitigation measures," British maritime security company Ambrey said, adding that it assessed vessels calling at Saudi Arabian ports "were at high risk".Yanbu continues to load crude onto tankers that were already operating in the Red Sea or had entered through the Suez Canal, the Reuters report said.Vessel-tracking data indicated that the tanker Olympic Luck, which had transited the Suez Canal into the Red Sea, remained en route to Yanbu, along with several other nearby vessels. However, since Tuesday, most tankers either sailing through the Red Sea or loading at Yanbu have switched off their transponders.Routing vessels through the Suez Canal instead of allowing them to leave the Red Sea via the Bab el-Mandeb Strait would significantly lengthen voyages to Asian destinations, as ships would need to transit the Mediterranean before sailing around Africa."While an actual blockade seems unlikely given the resources required for such an undertaking, a step-up in hostilities could see Houthis targeting Saudi-associated ships transiting the Bab el-Mandeb strait," ship broker Clarksons said in a note on Tuesday.Clarksons noted that, in recent months, an average of 10 crude tankers had been passing through the Bab el-Mandeb each day."However, should Houthis affect traffic through the region, we could see a reshuffling of crude cargoes in which Yanbu volumes are increasingly directed towards Europe."Because fully loaded VLCCs cannot pass through the Suez Canal at full draft, they are required to offload part of their cargo, which can then be transported across Egypt via the SUMED pipeline before being reloaded in the Mediterranean.
Article Summary: Three tankers carrying Saudi Arabia crude oil that were bound for China and India reversed course in the Red Sea on Tuesday. The change in route followed a warning issued by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia, according to a Reuters report. The Houthis control northern Yemen, including the coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Article Title: Pharma stocks bleed after Trump announces up to 200% tariff on generic drugs; Aurobindo, Sun Pharma & Cipla slide over 3%
Article Text:
Trump’s announcement



Why it matters for Indian drugmakers

Pharmaceutical stocks came under pressure on Wednesday after US President Donald Trump unveiled a phased tariff plan for imported generic medicines, raising concerns over the long-term outlook for one of the industry's biggest export markets.The sell-off came even though the proposal gives generic drugmakers a two-year tariff-free window before steep duties are introduced.Nifty Pharma index fell nearly 2% in opening trade as investors weighed the potential impact of tariffs that would eventually rise to 200%.After the news, shares of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Cipla, Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Lupin and Aurobindo Pharma landed among the biggest losers in early trade.Aurobindo Pharma tumbled 3.48% or 54.95 points to 1525.50. Sun Pharma declined to 1943.45, shedding 18.70 points or 0.95% on BSE, while Cipla fell 2.5% to Rs 1,396 per share. Lupin also dropped 2.5% to Rs 2,452, while Dr Reddy's Laboratories slipped more than 1% to Rs 1,185. Zydus, Alkem Laboratories and Torrent Pharmaceuticals also declined by up to 2%.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that all generic drugs being brought into the US will have no tariffs for two years.Following which, the tariff will be raised to 100% from August 1, 2028 and then to 200% by August 1, 2029.The phased tariff plan is intended to encourage pharmaceutical companies to establish manufacturing plants and related infrastructure in the US during the transition period. Companies that do not localise production would eventually face higher import duties under the administration's broader "America First" manufacturing agenda.The announcement also marks a shift in the administration's approach. Earlier tariff measures in the pharmaceutical sector targeted branded and patented medicines, while generic drugs remained outside the scope of those duties. That policy remains unchanged.US remains an important market for Indian pharmaceutical giants, with generic medicines accounting for nearly 90% of prescriptions in the country.The two-year tariff-free period offers Indian exporters additional time to reassess their supply chains and investment plans. While the immediate impact on exports is expected to be limited, tariffs of 100% and later 200% could significantly alter the economics of supplying generic medicines to the US for companies that do not strengthen their manufacturing presence there.India's pharmaceutical industry has been closely tracking changes in US trade policy amid concerns about potential tariffs on medicines. Industry executives have said India's cost-efficient manufacturing ecosystem remains globally competitive, although prolonged tariff barriers could prompt companies to expand manufacturing capacity in the US or rely more on contract manufacturing partnerships to maintain access to the market.Among Indian drugmakers, Aurobindo Pharma has a substantial manufacturing presence in the US. Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Lupin, Cipla and Zydus Lifesciences also have manufacturing operations there.Alkem Laboratories and Torrent Pharmaceuticals remain largely dependent on manufacturing facilities in India and have limited exposure to US generics in terms of cash flow generation. Biocon manufactures its biosimilar and generic products from facilities in India and Malaysia, while Senores Pharmaceuticals has a local manufacturing presence serving the US generics market.
Article Summary: Nifty Pharma index fell nearly 2% in opening trade as investors weighed potential impact of tariffs that would eventually rise to 200%. Shares of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Cipla, Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Lupin and Aurobindo Pharma landed among the biggest losers in early trade.

Article Title: Healthcare sector contests USTR claim on excess capacity
Article Text: After the US launched Section 301 investigations into structural excess capacity across several countries including India, targeting manufacturing sectors, domestic pharma and medical device sectors have submitted their positions amid such potential concerns.The sectors have argued that domestic manufacturers neither create structural excess capacity nor resort to market-distorting pricing practices, sources told TOI.During discussions with the US side, the pharma industry argued that domestic capacity has evolved to serve global demand for affordable medicines rather than any single market, they added.The industry is understood to have conveyed to the US side that India accounts for about 20% of global generic medicine supplies by volume, exports pharmaceuticals worth nearly $30 billion annually, while also serving a domestic market of a similar size. The US, its largest export destination, accounts for around $10 billion, or about one-third of exports, with Indian companies supplying nearly 40% of generic prescriptions dispensed there. It also emphasised India’s competitive pricing is driven by scale and manufacturing efficiencies, rather than from unfair market practices.Further, the medical devices industry has pushed back against Washington’s claims saying the US continues to be India’s largest supplier in medical devices, while India’s exports to the country are insignificant.Domestic medical device exports to the US remain relatively modest at around Rs 6,000 crore annually, while US imports are pegged almost triple at over Rs 16,000 crore.The industry has argued that there is no evidence of structural excess capacity in the sector, with manufacturing capacity expanding in response to domestic demand. "The sector remains heavily import-dependent for high-end devices, which account for about 80% of demand, while domestic manufacturers are concentrated in consumables, disposables and select implantable devices’’, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry said.The industry has argued that capacity expansion in India’s medical device sector is market-driven and export-oriented, with no reliance on distortionary subsidies or policies, and has urged the USTR to recognise the sector’s ecosystem before taking any unilateral action under Section 301.Media reports suggest govt has pushed back against the US claims on certain key sectors during the bilateral trade talks.
Article Summary: The sectors have argued that domestic manufacturers neither create structural excess capacity nor resort to market-distorting pricing practices. The industry is understood to have conveyed to the US side that India accounts for about 20% of global generic medicine supplies by volume, exports pharmaceuticals worth nearly $30 billion annually.

Article Title: Gabriel acquires promoter stake in JV, family holding up at 68%
Article Text: MUMBAI: Anand Group, the over $3 billion auto components conglomerate, is undertaking two linked transactions worth about Rs 3,180 crore through listed flagship Gabriel India that will lift promoter Anjali Singh and family's stake in the company to 68% and deepen its footprint in the sector.Gabriel will buy out the Singh family's 29% stake in HL Mando Anand India for Rs 2,231 crore. The family holds the stake through Asia Investments (AI), also a Gabriel promoter entity. South Korea's HL Group holds the remaining 71%.Gabriel will pay Rs 350 crore in cash to AI and issue shares worth Rs 1,881 crore for the balance, at an allotment price of Rs 1,305.89 apiece. Gabriel's scrip closed at Rs 1,493.4 on the BSE on Tuesday. The share issuance will take the Singh family's stake in Gabriel to 68%, from 64% currently.Separately, Gabriel will acquire a "30% minus one share" in HL Klemove India, an autonomous driving solutions maker owned by HL Group, for Rs 945 crore - giving the company its entry into the segment. HL will retain "70% plus one share" in HL Klemove after the sale.Anand Group was founded by Singh's father, Deep Anand, in 1961. He set up Gabriel in collaboration with the US's Maremont Corporation, now Gabriel Ride Control, to manufacture shock absorbers in Mumbai. Singh succeeded her father as group head in February 2011. She and her husband, Jaisal Singh, also founded safari brand Sujan in Rajasthan.
Article Summary: Anand Group, the over $3 billion auto components conglomerate, is undertaking two linked transactions worth about Rs 3,180 crore. Gabriel will buy out the Singh family's 29% stake in HL Mando Anand India for Rs 2,231 crore. The family holds the stake through Asia Investments (AI), also a Gabriel promoter entity.

Article Title: Boards look beyond tested playbook to hire leaders
Article Text:
This is reflective of an underlying shift in terms of how workplaces are approaching leadership hiring

MUMBAI: Fintech startup Cred founder Kunal Shah 's appointment as the head of WhatsApp got everyone talking on social media. Much of the discourse was around a Philosophy graduate making it to the top echelons of the tech world.Shah, of course, has had the experience of building and running new-age tech ventures and Meta roped in him to help monetise the business in India, WhatsApp's biggest market. But all said and done, Shah's appointment is somewhat unconventional--it doesn't follow the typical corporate hiring script of boards mandating companies to hire leaders with a certain kind of educational background or professional experience.Shah is among a handful of such Indian-origin leaders--think Leena Nair who went on to become the CEO of French luxury fashion house Chanel from Unilever where she held the CHRO's office; or Nikhil Ravishankar who was elevated to CEO at Air New Zealand despite having a career entirely in digital transformation and consulting.This is reflective of an underlying shift in terms of how workplaces are approaching leadership hiring."Executive search has always worked on the dominant logic of linearity. You hired a retail veteran to run a retail giant, a banker to lead a bank. But that framework is eroding....A part of what's driving this is the nature of disruption itself," said Anagh Sood, operating partner at executive search firm Positive Moves.Some of the most well-known companies-Amazon, Uber, Netflix, were not built by domain experts. The products that redefined entire industries came from outsiders willing to question the status quo. Boards are starting to apply the same logic to their corner offices and broader leadership hiring, said Sood.Industries themselves are no longer operating in neat, isolated silos. Today, a luxury brand is essentially a digital media platform and a technology firm is ultimately a consumer habit engine, said Anjali Raghuvanshi, chief people officer, Randstad India & Global Capability Centre. "Boards are finally prioritising perspective over pedigree. There is a healthy realisation that technical skills have a shelf life but acute emotional intelligence, the ability to manage chaos, and deep curiosity do not," said Raghuvanshi.There could be risks attached to hiring people from non-traditional backgrounds but at the same time, boards want leaders who can deal with ambiguity which defines the current business landscape, said Sankalp Mohanty, partner, human capital consulting at Deloitte India.For companies, such a non-linear approach helps widen the talent pool besides infusing new ideas, said Himanshu Priyadarshi, partner and associate director at Boston Consulting Group (BCG). "However, it requires rethinking talent frameworks to be effective at scale," said Priyadarshi.
Article Summary: Kunal Shah's appointment as the head of WhatsApp got everyone talking on social media. Shah is among a handful of such Indian-origin leaders--think Leena Nair who went on to become the CEO of French luxury fashion house Chanel from Unilever where she held the CHRO's office.

Article Title: JSW Group in talks to buy stake in Volkswagen India
Article Text:
Sajjan Jindal-led conglomerate is reportedly seeking a majority stake in the venture

Volkswagen is in advanced discussions with India's JSW Group, said people familiar with the matter, as the German automaker seeks an ally to infuse fresh capital and bolster its local unit in the world's third-largest auto market. The two sides are working toward a potential agreement in the coming weeks involving JSW making an investment in closely held Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, the people said, asking not to be identified as the discussions are confidential.The Sajjan Jindal-led conglomerate is seeking a majority stake in the venture, the people added.While top executives from Volkswagen and JSW have held meetings recently, several sticking points remain unresolved, including a valuation for the deal and JSW and Volkswagen's capital investments, the people said.The transaction, if finalised, will cap Volkswagen's years-long hunt for a local Indian partner. The German manufacturer has struggled to build scale in India even after operating in the country for more than two decades. For the steel-to-electric vehicles conglomerate JSW, a deal would provide access to Volkswagen's vehicle platforms and a springboard for further potential cooperation globally with a well-established European carmaker.Volkswagen is constantly evaluating new business opportunities to implement its strategy in India, which is an important market for Skoda Auto's global growth plans, a company spokesperson said in an email, while declining to comment on any discussions with JSW. A JSW spokesperson did not respond to an emailed request for comments on the deal.The Volkswagen group, across its brands, makes up about 2.5% of India's passenger vehicle market.Volkswagen has become more willing to cede control of its India unit as it grapples with a difficult turnaround globally, the people familiar with the talks said. Although the Indian unit has posted a jump in profit for the year ended March 31, they said the European parent is growing wary of funding the business without a local partner to share the load.(This is a Bloomberg story)
Article Summary: Volkswagen is in advanced discussions with India's JSW Group, said people familiar with the matter. The two sides are working toward a potential agreement in the coming weeks involving JSW making an investment in closely held Skoda Auto Volkswagen India. The Sajjan Jindal-led conglomerate is seeking a majority stake in the venture.

Article Title: Maruti to raise prices by up to Rs 30k from August
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Maruti Suzuki India, the country's largest carmaker, will increase prices across its passenger vehicle lineup by up to Rs 30,000 from Aug, becoming the latest automaker to pass on rising manufacturing costs to buyers.In a stock exchange filing on Tuesday, it cited persistent increases in production expenses that had left it with little choice but to revise prices. Maruti said it had spent the past several months trying to offset higher expenses through internal efficiency measures and cost optimisation initiatives.Tata Motors implemented a price increase of up to 1.5% across its passenger vehicle range, including electric vehicles, from July 1.
Article Summary: Maruti Suzuki India, the country's largest carmaker, will increase prices across its passenger vehicle lineup by up to Rs 30,000 from Aug. It cited persistent increases in production expenses that had left it with little choice but to revise prices.

Article Title: Karnataka sees fastest FDI rise among major states
Article Text:
Karnataka saw FDI flows nearly double to $13 billion

Maharashtra FDI declines

NEW DELHI: Karnataka saw FDI flows nearly double to $13 billion during the last financial year as tech investors and global capability centres (GCCs) flocked to India's Silicon Valley, while Maharashtra, the top destination, saw a dip in inflows after two years.Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Punjab were among states that saw a significant increase in equity inflows, while Telangana saw a decline, latest official data shared in Parliament on Tuesday showed (see graphic). Gujarat was flat at $5.7 billion, also retaining the third spot among states.FDI comprises equity and reinvested earnings of companies but the data shared by govt was on the former. Last year, equity inflows into India rose 17.6% to $58 billion.A large part of the investments were driven by tech companies with money flowing into data centres and GCCs as well as investments into e-commerce companies such as Amazon and Flipkart. Sector wise data showed computer software and hardware ($13.9 billion) along with services sector ($10 billion) that includes finance, banking, insurance etc saw robust growth in FY26 and cornered nearly 40% of the total FDI inflows ($58.8 billion).Notably, food processing industry saw FDI grow nearly six times to $3 billion, while others like drugs and pharmaceuticals ($1.9 billion), automobile industry ($ 2.5 billion) and education ($1.3 billion) also saw robust growth.Meanwhile, FDI in air transport fell nearly 70% to $383 million, whereas the electronics sector saw FDI nearly halve to $1.1 billion.
Article Summary: Karnataka saw FDI flows nearly double to $13 billion during the last financial year. Maharashtra, the top destination, saw a dip in inflows after two years. Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Punjab were among states that saw significant increase in equity inflows.

Article Title: MMU ET 2026 results released as online counselling and seat allotment process set to begin
Article Text:
MMU ET 2026 result declared as counselling process begins with scorecards now available for qualified candidates online

MMU ET 2026 result

:

How to check the result

Counselling process to begin soon

Admission timeline and examination details

Registration trends and admission framework

The Marwar Medical University Entrance Test (MMU ET) 2026 result was officially declared on July 20, 2026. Candidates who appeared for the entrance examination on July 3, 2026 can now access their scores and download their scorecards through the official candidate portal using their registered login credentials. The university has also advised applicants to follow updates through its official website.The declaration of results marks the completion of the examination and evaluation process for this admission cycle. With scorecards now available, the admission process will move to the online counselling stage, where eligible candidates will participate in choice filling and seat allotment for available programmes.Candidates can download their MMU ET 2026 scorecard by logging into the MMU ET Application Index Portal with their registered credentials. The university has also made result-related notifications available through its official website. Applicants are advised to save a copy of the scorecard, as it will be required during subsequent admission formalities.Online counselling, including choice filling and seat allotment, is scheduled to commence in the fourth week of July 2026.Candidates should keep their original MMU ET scorecard, admit card, academic certificates and category certificates ready for document verification. These documents will be required during the admission process before seat confirmation.The MMU ET 2026 application process opened on May 21 and concluded on June 14, followed by the correction window on June 15 and 16. Exam city details were released on June 24, while admit cards became available on June 28. The examination was conducted on July 3. The provisional answer key was issued on July 5, and candidates could submit objections between July 6 and 8 before the result declaration on July 20.Admission data for the current cycle indicate that the examination recorded fewer applications than comparable statewide admission cycles. However, more than 92 per cent of registered candidates appeared for the test across regional examination centres. Initial response analysis placed 74 marks and above as a safe benchmark for General category aspirants seeking leading seats, while over 65 per cent of qualified candidates scored between 55 and 70 marks. Marwar Medical University, Jodhpur functions as a State Government University under the Marwar Medical University Act, with regulated fee provisions and statutory reservation policies for Rajasthan domicile candidates.
Article Summary: The Marwar Medical University Entrance Test (MMU ET) 2026 result was officially declared on July 20, 2026. Candidates who appeared for the entrance examination can now access their scores and download their scorecards through the official candidate portal using their registered login credentials. The university has also advised applicants to follow updates through its official website.

Article Title: PNB LBO Recruitment 2026: Applications for 545 Local Bank Officer posts begin at pnb.bank.in; check eligibility and selection process
Article Text:
PNB Bank LBO Recruitment 2026 begins for 545 vacancies; applications open until August 09, 2026 nationwide

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026

:

Eligibility criteria and age limit

•

•

Selection process and examination pattern

Application fee and submission process

Punjab National Bank (PNB) has invited online applications for the recruitment of 545 Local Bank Officer (LBO) posts under Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I). The recruitment drive is being conducted for vacancies across multiple states, with applications being accepted through the bank's official website from July 20, 2026 to August 09, 2026.Candidates applying for the posts must hold a graduation degree, possess at least one year of banking experience and demonstrate proficiency in the local language of the state for which they are seeking appointment. The selected candidates will be posted only in the state for which they apply. The pay scale for the post ranges from ?48,480 to ?85,920.Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years of age as on July 01, 2026. Age relaxation will be available in accordance with Government of India rules. SC and ST candidates are eligible for five years of relaxation, OBC (NCL) candidates for three years, PwBD candidates for 10 years, ex-servicemen for five years and 1984 riot-affected persons for five years.The recruitment has announced vacancies across Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura, taking the total number of posts to 545.The selection process comprises an online written examination, document screening, Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT), personal interview, final merit list and document verification.The online examination will carry 150 questions for 150 marks with a total duration of 180 minutes. The paper will include Reasoning and Computer Aptitude, Data Analysis and Interpretation, English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, and General, Economy and Banking Awareness. A deduction of 0.25 marks will apply for every incorrect response.The application fee has been fixed at Rs 59, including GST, for SC, ST and PwBD candidates, while General, OBC and EWS candidates are required to pay Rs 1,180, including GST.To apply, candidates need to register with a valid email ID and mobile number, complete the online application form, upload the required documents, photograph and signature, pay the prescribed fee online and submit the application. The selected candidates will be posted only in the state for which they apply.

Article Title: BCI draft Bill seeks higher enrolment fee, law admission changes and professional development programmes
Article Text:
BCI proposes Rs 22,500 advocate enrolment fee alongside sweeping legal education reforms under draft amendment Bill. (AI Image)

Proposed fee revision and concessions

Wider

legal education reforms

proposed

Focus on continuing legal education

(Witn inputs from Bar and Bench)

NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has proposed increasing the statutory enrolment fee for aspiring advocates from Rs 750 to Rs 22,500 under the Draft Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which has been released for public consultation. The proposal also outlines a series of reforms covering legal education, advocate training, institutional oversight and professional development.Under the draft, Section 24 of the Advocates Act, 1961 would be amended to revise the enrolment fee to Rs 18,000 payable to the concerned State Bar Council and Rs 4,500 to the Bar Council of India. The BCI has invited suggestions from stakeholders, including State Bar Councils, bar associations, law universities, centres of legal education and law firms, until 3 pm on July 31, 2026.According to the draft, the revised fee has been proposed following Supreme Court judgments in Gaurav Kumar v Union of India and Pankaj Sinha v Bar Council of India. The BCI noted that the existing statutory enrolment fee has remained unchanged since 1993 despite expanded institutional responsibilities linked to advocate enrolment.The explanatory note states that the revised fee would support verification of educational qualifications and identity, maintenance of physical and digital enrolment records, issuance of enrolment certificates, advocate welfare measures including insurance and mediclaim, professional development programmes, establishment of a National Legal Academy and other institutional services.The draft also proposes that candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and persons with benchmark disabilities will be required to pay only one-fourth of the prescribed enrolment fee.The draft Bill seeks to empower the BCI to conduct entrance examinations for admission to law degree programmes, prescribe minimum admission qualifications, frame rules for the All India Bar Examination, and recognise legal education institutions as well as foreign law qualifications.It also proposes expanding the Legal Education Committee from 10 members to 25 members. The reconstituted body would include representatives from the judiciary, government, universities, legal academia and the legal profession.The draft proposes making continuing legal education a statutory function of both the BCI and State Bar Councils. Professional development programmes may include constitutional law, corporate and commercial law, arbitration, artificial intelligence, cyber law, taxation, insolvency, international legal practice, and trial and appellate advocacy.The BCI said these programmes are intended to strengthen advocates' professional capabilities and expand learning opportunities without creating unnecessary burdens on practitioners.
Article Summary: The Bar Council of India has proposed increasing the statutory enrolment fee for aspiring advocates from Rs 750 to Rs 22,500. The proposal also outlines a series of reforms covering legal education, advocate training, institutional oversight and professional development. The BCI has invited suggestions from stakeholders, including State Bar Councils, bar associations, law universities, centres of legal education and law firms.

Article Title: Trump announces 0% tariff on generic medicines for two years; 200% thereafter
Article Text:
Trump said the move was intended to encourage companies to manufacture generic medicines domestically

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced a phased tariff regime on imported generic medicines, saying they will continue to enter the United States duty-free for two years and then steep tariff hikes aimed at bringing pharmaceutical manufacturing back to the country.Announcing the policy, Trump said the move was intended to encourage companies to manufacture generic medicines domestically."Effective August 1st, 2026, all Generic Drugs being brought into the United States will continue to have a TARIFF of ZERO PERCENT for a two year period of time, after which the TARIFF will be raised to 100% for a one year period of time, and 200% thereafter. This is done in order to RESHORE Generic Pharmaceutical Production into America, with a penalty to those Companies that decide not to build Plant and Equipment within the stated period of time given to them. The objective of this Policy is to protect the people of the United States," Trump said on Truth Social.He added that the policy for "Patented, Branded, or Innovative Drugs" would remain unchanged, claiming it had been successful. Trump also said pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities were "being built, at a level never seen before, all over the United States of America."Generic medicines account for more than 90% of prescriptions dispensed in the United States, according to the US Food and Drug Administration.The announcement follows Trump's broader push to increase domestic pharmaceutical production and lower drug prices through his "most-favored-nation" pricing policy. Last year, major drugmakers reached agreements with the US government that exempted billions of dollars' worth of medicines from tariffs, while Trump also imposed tariffs on imported branded pharmaceuticals unless manufacturers agreed to pricing deals or committed to producing them in the US.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced a phased tariff regime on imported generic medicines. He said they will continue to enter the United States duty-free for two years and then steep tariff hikes. Trump said the move was intended to encourage companies to manufacture generic medicines domestically.

Article Title: US stock market today: AI stocks extend rally; Brent crude prices go above $90
Article Text:
Artificial intelligence-related stocks remained the primary drivers of the market, building on the previous session's recovery after suffering sharp declines last week.



Brent crude goes above $90

US stock market today: Wall Street extended its gains on Tuesday, supported by another strong rally in shares of chipmakers and other companies that have benefited from the artificial intelligence boom. Artificial intelligence-related stocks remained the primary drivers of the market, building on the previous session's recovery after suffering sharp declines last week.The S&P 500 advanced 0.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 219 points, or 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite outperformed, rising 0.8%.Following a prolonged surge fuelled by heavy investment in AI chips and data centres, these stocks have faced selling pressure in recent weeks amid concerns that valuations had become stretched. Investors are also questioning whether the current pace of AI-related spending can be sustained if the technology does not generate the anticipated improvements in profitability and productivity, according to an AP report.Micron Technology climbed 7.8%, adding to Monday's 1.9% gain after having fallen 13.3% during the previous week.Nvidia rose 1.5% after revealing that it holds a 9.3% stake in Nebius, a Dutch artificial intelligence cloud company.Along with Micron, Nvidia provided the biggest boost to the S&P 500.The advance in equities came despite another increase in oil prices. Brent crude climbed above $90 a barrel as hostilities between the United States and Iran continued. The global benchmark rose 1.9% to $90.92 a barrel, compared with levels below $72 earlier this month, roughly where it had been before the Iran conflict began.The continued rise in crude prices has renewed concerns that inflation could accelerate again after showing signs of easing more quickly than economists had anticipated. Such a development could prompt the Federal Reserve and other central banks to raise interest rates further, a move that would weigh on economic growth and put pressure on stock prices and other asset classes.The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note edged up to 4.62% from 4.60% at Monday's close. Before the outbreak of the Iran conflict, the yield had stood at 3.97%.On Wall Street, a series of better-than-expected quarterly earnings from major US companies helped lift equities despite the headwinds created by rising oil prices and higher bond yields.Shares of 3M surged 8.7% after the industrial conglomerate reported quarterly profit and revenue that exceeded analysts' estimates. The company also upgraded its full-year 2026 profit outlook.European markets were mixed, with most benchmarks posting only modest moves. In the UK, the FTSE 100 advanced 0.2% as newly appointed Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired his first Cabinet meeting.Asian equities recorded larger swings. South Korea's Kospi climbed 3.6%, driven by strong gains in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, two companies that have benefited significantly from the AI boom. Although the Kospi has declined 20% during July, it remains up 60% for the year so far.Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 3.3% after reopening following Monday's holiday. Shanghai's benchmark index gained 1.8%, while Hong Kong's market slipped marginally, ending less than 0.1% lower.
Article Summary: The S&P 500 advanced 0.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 219 points, or 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite outperformed, rising 0.8%. Artificial intelligence-related stocks remained the primary drivers of the market, building on the previous session's recovery.

Article Title: The future of flying? US moves to fast-track air taxis, supersonic planes and drone expansion
Article Text:
Air taxi (representative image)

FAA using pilot programme to prepare for air taxi rollout

Industry working towards commercial operations

FAA also pushing to revive supersonic travel

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is stepping up efforts to support the deployment of air taxis, supersonic passenger aircraft, drones and commercial space launches, as it looks to modernise aviation regulations and accelerate the adoption of next-generation technologies.Speaking to Reuters at the Farnborough International Airshow, FAA deputy administrator Chris Rocheleau said the agency was working to streamline certification and regulatory processes while allowing companies greater flexibility to innovate."We want to make sure that we're not being too prescriptive in those standards, and that we're letting the industry drive the innovation," Rocheleau said.The FAA launched an electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program last year to help manufacturers begin deploying the new class of aircraft.The programme involves eight partner companies across 26 US states, with data gathered from the trials expected to support future certification efforts."The whole idea behind this is to take this new technology, these new aircraft, and put them into the national airstream in a safe and efficient manner," Rocheleau said.Air taxi developers are racing to obtain regulatory approval for eVTOL aircraft, which are designed to take off and land vertically and could eventually be used for short urban trips and airport transfers, offering an alternative to congested roads.Archer Aviation CEO Adam Goldstein compared the rollout of air taxis to Google's self-driving vehicle programme."I think the world has learned a lot in how the autonomous vehicles have launched," Goldstein told Reuters.He said the FAA's pilot programme would allow companies to introduce the technology gradually."The FAA pilot program gives the eVTOL industry the ability to roll this out to a couple cities in a confined area that we can kind of work through the kinks in the system," Goldstein said.The push comes as aviation companies continue efforts to bring electric air taxis into commercial service.According to CNBC, aerospace company Beta Technologies recently completed the first test flights under the US government's eVTOL pilot programme, transporting manufactured organs between airports in Maryland and Virginia. The flights covered about 275 nautical miles.The pilot programme was launched under an executive order issued last year and covers eight projects across 26 states. Beta is currently participating in seven of those projects.The company expects certification of its conventional electric aircraft in 2027 and its eVTOL aircraft in 2028.Meanwhile, Archer Aviation, Beta Technologies and Macquarie Capital recently formed America's Consortium for Electric Skyways (ACES) to develop charging infrastructure for electric aircraft.The consortium plans to establish up to 250 interoperable charging sites across major US airports and metropolitan areas over the next decade to support commercial eVTOL operations.Beyond air taxis, the FAA is also moving to pave the way for the return of commercial supersonic passenger flights.The agency proposed the first of two new rules in June to lift a ban imposed in 1973 on supersonic flights over land.A second proposal will define acceptable noise limits during take-off, landing and supersonic cruise, with both rules expected to be finalised by mid-2027."We think the rules are old and outdated," Rocheleau told Reuters.Once the regulatory framework is in place, aircraft manufacturers will still need to obtain certification from the FAA and other aviation regulators before supersonic passenger aircraft can enter commercial service.The era of regular commercial supersonic travel ended in 2003, when the Concorde fleet operated by Air France and British Airways was retired after 27 years in service.Alongside air taxis and supersonic aircraft, the FAA is also working to expand drone operations and support a growing number of commercial space launches as part of its broader push to integrate emerging aviation technologies into the US airspace system.
Article Summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration is stepping up efforts to support the deployment of air taxis, supersonic passenger aircraft, drones and commercial space launches. FAA deputy administrator Chris Rocheleau said the agency was working to streamline certification and regulatory processes while allowing companies greater flexibility to innovate.

Article Title: New warning on oil: Goldman Sachs says crude prices could cross $120 if Strait of Hormuz disruptions continue
Article Text:
The analysts said the decline in global oil inventories during the second quarter has made the market more vulnerable to supply disruptions.

Goldman warns of crude at $120

Are Brent crude oil prices set to cross $120 per barrel again? According to Goldman Sachs Group Brent crude prices could climb above $120 a barrel in the fourth quarter if disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz continue. However, the investment bank said this is not its central forecast.Global energy markets have experienced significant volatility this month, with Brent crude climbing above $91 a barrel amid renewed hostilities between the US and Iran. Market sentiment has also been affected by threats from Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen to impose a blockade on Saudi shipments. Oil exports routed through the Red Sea have become especially important in helping crude cargoes from the disrupted Persian Gulf reach global buyers.In a note dated July 20, Goldman Sachs analysts said, “Escalation in the Middle East and the decline in estimated Persian Gulf flows to below 45% of pre-war levels have pushed oil prices back up.”According to a Bloomberg report, Goldman Sachs' base-case scenario assumes tensions in the Middle East ease, under which it expects Brent crude to average $80 a barrel in the fourth quarter and $75 a barrel next year. However, the analysts said the risks to this outlook remain “tilted to the upside” because of continued shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz and the possibility of further interruptions in the Red Sea.Also Read | Strait of Hormuz closure: Why crude oil prices haven’t spiralled out of control amid US-Iran conflict The analysts said the decline in global oil inventories during the second quarter has made the market more vulnerable to supply disruptions. However, weaker crude imports by China, along with higher demand elasticity, could moderate the extent of any price rally.For investors looking to protect themselves against prolonged geopolitical risks stemming from the Middle East and Russia, Goldman recommended taking a long position in the European diesel timespread for the period between December 2026 and March 2027.According to the analysts, diesel markets were already experiencing tight supply conditions before the conflict began. They noted that Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries were continuing, while additional risks to diesel supplies included hurricanes, extreme summer temperatures and delays in refinery maintenance.Brent crude futures were last trading at $88.54 a barrel. Earlier this year, during the initial stage of the US-Iran conflict, prices had climbed to above $126 a barrel in late April.
Article Summary: Goldman warns of crude at $120 per barrel in the fourth quarter if disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz continue. The investment bank said this is not its central forecast. Global energy markets have experienced significant volatility this month, with Brent crude climbing above $91 a barrel.

Article Title: 'Direct violation': Canada vows to protect workers after Trump slaps 50% tariffs on select goods
Article Text: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday said that US President Donald Trump 's decision to impose fresh 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods is a "direct violation" of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA).He further said that the government would continue to support the country's workers, businesses and families. His remarks came after Trump's latest tariffs targeted a range of Canadian exports, including motor vehicles, dairy products and alcoholic beverages, escalating trade tensions between the two neighbouring countries.In a statement posted on X, Carney said the latest US action was part of a series of unilateral trade measures that violated the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA)."This is the latest in a series of unilateral US trade actions that began with the US imposing a series of tariffs in direct violation of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA), the free trade agreement between Canada, the United States, and Mexico," he said."These include tariffs on the Canadian auto sector, in violation of CUSMA. Canada, as is its right, has merely matched those measures," Carney added referring to earlier US tariffs on Canada's automobile sector.The Canadian prime minister said the tariffs and repeated threats to Canada's sovereignty had united the country."In response to these measures and threats to Canadian sovereignty, provinces, territories, Canadians from coast to coast to coast have stood together, taking the necessary actions to support our economy and defend our workers, farmers, businesses, and families," he said.Carney said Canada had put forward detailed proposals to resolve the dispute and modernise CUSMA, adding that Ottawa remained open to negotiations."Recognising that the US has been transforming all of its trade relationships, including those covered under CUSMA, over the past 18 months, Canada has made a series of detailed and comprehensive proposals to resolve this dispute and to modernise CUSMA. We stand ready to intensify those discussions in the coming weeks," he said.Reiterating Canada's commitment to open markets, Carney said, "Canada believes in the benefits of free and fair trade, as evidenced by our new government signing more than 20 new economic and security partnerships. This trade dispute has raised costs for families, particularly in the US Canada stands ready to engage intensively to address outstanding issues with the US to the mutual benefit of our citizens."He added, "In all circumstances, Canada will work relentlessly and take any measures necessary to build our strength at home and to support Canadian workers, farmers, businesses, and families."Carney's remarks came after the White House announced a fresh round of 50% tariffs on several Canadian imports, saying the move was in response to what it described as Canada's "discriminatory treatment" of American products, particularly in the automobile, dairy and alcoholic beverage sectors.President Trump signed three proclamations under Section 338 of the Trade Act of 1930, with the tariffs set to take effect 30 days after signing, leaving room for possible negotiations, ANI reported. According to the White House, the new tariffs will apply to most Canadian goods but will exempt energy products, potash, fish and critical minerals.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump's decision to impose fresh 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods is a "direct violation" of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the government would continue to support the country's workers, businesses and families.

Article Title: Fresh threat to global oil supply: Saudi Arabia’s crude exports at risk as Yemen’s Houthis look to impose maritime blockade
Article Text:
Saudi Arabia has rerouted its crude exports through the Red Sea port of Yanbu after Hormuz disruptions. (Satellite image of Bab-el-Mandeb Strait - source Reuters)

Bab el-Mandeb Strait: Key shipping chokepoint

Saudi Arabia’s crude exports face fresh threats

Saudi Crude Exports From Yanbu Are Up

After the Strait of Hormuz disruptions, a fresh threat to the world's oil supply has emerged with the Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen announcing a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia. This has raised concerns over the movement of millions of barrels of crude oil that Saudi Arabia exports through the Red Sea.According to the group, the move is a response to what it describes as Saudi Arabia's siege of Yemen's capital, Sana'a. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a video posted on his X account on Monday that the blockade on Saudi vessels would take effect immediately.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fluctuated on Monday amid expectations of both further escalation and possible de-escalation in the conflict. As of 2:06 p.m. in London, it was trading 0.2% higher at $88.23 a barrel.Relations between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have deteriorated since last week after Riyadh carried out an attack on Sana'a airport. The Houthis responded by striking an airport in southern Saudi Arabia, marking the most serious escalation between the two sides since the 2022 ceasefire.The development adds another layer of uncertainty to oil supplies from the Middle East.Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz—through which nearly one-fifth of global oil supplies moved before the US-led conflict with Iran—remains close to a halt as Tehran and Washington continue exchanging retaliatory attacks.Any disruption to Red Sea shipments, currently the primary route for Saudi Arabia's crude exports, would further intensify the impact of the conflict on global oil trade.Following the outbreak of the war and Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia rerouted its crude exports through the Red Sea port of Yanbu.Shipments from the port climbed to a record 4.19 million barrels per day last month, helping ease pressure on global supplies. However, the route remains vulnerable because tankers sailing through the Red Sea continue to face the threat of attacks from Houthi militants, who have targeted commercial vessels there in the past.In late 2023, the Houthis disrupted maritime traffic around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea for several months. Shipping through the strategic waterway was reduced to almost a standstill, forcing vessels to abandon the shortest maritime route linking Asia and Europe.
Article Summary: The Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen has announced a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia. This has raised concerns over the movement of millions of barrels of crude oil that Saudi Arabia exports through the Red Sea. Relations between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have deteriorated since last week after Riyadh carried out an attack on Sana'a airport.

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street back in green; AI-related, chipmaker stocks rebound
Article Text:
AI-linked stocks have faced sustained selling pressure in recent weeks amid concerns that valuations had risen too rapidly.

US stock market today: Wall Street rebounded on Monday as shares of chipmakers and other companies that have benefited from the artificial intelligence boom recovered after recent sharp declines.The S&P 500 advanced 0.6%, following its first weekly loss in three weeks and only its third weekly decline since the end of March. As of 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had gained 122 points, or 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1%.Nvidia rose 1.9%, helping lift the broader market after being the biggest drag on the S&P 500 during Friday's session. Sandisk also recovered, jumping 6.7% after sliding 29% over the previous week.AI-linked stocks have faced sustained selling pressure in recent weeks amid concerns that valuations had risen too rapidly during the excitement surrounding artificial intelligence.While companies supplying AI chips and data centres continue to generate billions of dollars in revenue as customers ramp up spending, investors remain concerned that such investment could slow if AI fails to deliver the expected gains in profitability and productivity.Investors may soon receive fresh indications on that front as several of the largest AI spenders prepare to announce quarterly results. Alphabet is scheduled to report on Wednesday, when it will disclose its spring-quarter earnings and provide updates on its artificial intelligence initiatives.The earnings season is also placing pressure on companies across industries—not just technology—to deliver strong profit growth for the spring quarter, as lofty share prices will need to be supported by solid financial performance. Major stock indices remain close to record highs despite recent volatility driven by AI-related stocks.AMC Entertainment surged 11.6% after reporting quarterly revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations. The cinema chain also said some of its theatres in Los Angeles and other cities screened The Odyssey continuously for more than 85 hours between Thursday and Sunday to meet strong demand.Domino's Pizza gained 4.2% after posting stronger-than-expected spring-quarter revenue. CEO Russell Weiner said the company recorded growth in both carryout and delivery orders despite the broader industry continuing “to face pressure on consumer demand.”Much of that strain on consumer spending continues to stem from elevated inflation, driven largely by high fuel prices. Although last month's inflation reading came in below economists' expectations, rising oil prices could push inflation higher again if the current trend persists.Earlier this month, Brent crude had fallen below $72 a barrel, returning to roughly the level seen before the Iran conflict began. However, prices have climbed again as hostilities in the Middle East continue.During Monday's trading, Brent crude fluctuated sharply between about $86 and $91 a barrel before easing 0.4% to $87.76.Concerns over rising oil prices and persistent inflation have also pushed Treasury yields higher, raising fears that tighter financial conditions could slow economic growth and weigh on stocks and other asset prices.The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note edged up to 4.56% from 4.55% at Friday's close and has risen from 3.97% before the outbreak of the Iran conflict. Higher bond yields have already lifted the average rate on 30-year mortgages to its highest level in almost a year.European equity markets traded modestly lower.Losses were more pronounced across Asia, where South Korea's Kospi declined 4.5%. The benchmark has experienced particularly large swings because of its heavy exposure to technology giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, both major beneficiaries of the AI boom.
Article Summary: The S&P 500 advanced 0.6%, following its first weekly loss in three weeks and only its third weekly decline since the end of March. As of 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had gained 122 points, or 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1%.

Article Title: Despite Trump-Xi agreement, China’s rare earth magnet exports to US remain 20% below pre-trade war levels
Article Text:
Shipments of these key industrial components to the US during the first six months of the year were roughly 20% lower than the average recorded between 2022 and 2024. (Reuters photo)

China exports fewer magnets to US

China's exports of rare-earth magnets to the United States continue to remain significantly below levels recorded before the trade conflict, despite the truce reached last year.
